description:
Creates a NEW TabTree mind map from a markdown outline (#/## headings, bullet lists indented by 2 spaces, [x]/[ ] checkboxes, [title](url) links, and " @a:<id>" / " @e:<emoji>" at the end of a line for an illustration). The first top-level line becomes the centre. SCREENSHOTS: pass `images` — a list of { target, file } where `file` is the path of a PNG/JPEG on this machine (a screenshot you saved) and `target` the exact text of the node it goes on; the picture is re-encoded to fit and drawn as the node's cover.

PROJECT — when the user wants to run a project, a product, a launch or a plan of bets (not a one-off mind map), create it with `format: "projet"`: one tree that holds the vision, the objectives, the epics as bets you settle, their cards and the sprints. TabTree recognises the first-level branches by their leading emoji. Write it like this (an attribute is its own line "Name: value"):
# 🗂 <Project name>
- Description: one sentence — what ships, for whom, why now
- Vision: the world once it has worked, no numbers
- Mission: what ships by when, with the one number that proves it
- Sprint length: 2 weeks          (optional — the planned rhythm)
- Sprints start: 2026-11-02       (optional — the first sprint's first day)
- 🎯 Objectives
  - O1 — the outcome, by a date
    - [ ] KR1 — a number with its target
- 🧱 Epics
  - F · Foundations
    - Hypothesis: what we believe is true and justifies the epic
    - Goal: the number that settles it
    - Signal: the indicator, and where it is read
    - Verdict: untested             (untested | testing | validated | invalidated)
    - Impact: 4                     (optional, 1–5; with Confidence and Effort → ICE = Impact × Confidence × (6 − Effort))
    - Confidence: 3
    - Effort: 2
    - [ ] F01 · a card, a deliverable in a few days @todo
- 📚 Knowledge
  - [Company knowledge](map:<file>)
- 📝 Decisions
  - 2026-10-26 — the decision, who took it, and the gate that reopens it
Pass `columns` to put the cards on the project's kanban — usually [{ id:"backlog", name:"Backlog" }, { id:"todo", name:"To do" }, { id:"doing", name:"Doing", wip:4 }, { id:"done", name:"Done", done:true }] — and end a card's line with " @<column id>" ("@todo"); a project card without a marker goes to the first column. Cards in Backlog are not committed; everything else is the current sprint. Each objective's gauge is its ticked KRs; each epic shows its verdict as a coloured dot. Other formats: okr, pv (meeting minutes), org (org chart), radial, outline, oneside, timeline, suivi (completion rate on every branch).

Writes a .tabtree file into the backup folder; the user pulls it into the app from the 🛟 menu.

columns.description: Optional kanban columns, left to right — the cards then live on a board too (the same tree, another view). Give each an `id` and end a card's line with " @<id>" to place it ("- [ ] F01 · Instrument the funnel @todo"); mark ONE column done:true (a card placed there is ticked). In format projet, an epic's card without a marker goes to the first column. 12 max.

id.description: Short id used by the " @<id>" line marker, e.g. backlog, todo, doing, done (letters, digits, - or _)

dates.description: Optional start/due days on nodes — what the Gantt view draws (and what the kanban and calendar show). One entry per node.

folder.description: Optional TabTree folder. A NAME ("From Claude") or a full PATH ("Ai4X / Programmes"). When several folders share a name, the shallowest is used and the answer says which — pass the full path to choose another.

format.description: Optional living format — projet (a project: vision, objectives, epics as bets, cards, sprints — see the shape above), okr, pv (meeting minutes), org (org chart), radial, outline, oneside, timeline, suivi (tracking). Omit for a plain mind map. The user can change it later; Cmd+Z undoes it.

images.description: Optional screenshots, one per node: { target, file } or { target, data }. `target` = the exact text of a line of the outline (or "Ancestor > Node" when the wording repeats); `file` = full path of a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF on this machine (take the screenshot, save it, pass the path); `data` = a data:image/… URL instead of a file. The image is re-encoded to about 840 px and becomes the node's cover picture (it replaces any @a:/@e: illustration on that node). 60 max.

file.description: Path of the image file on this machine

markdown.description: Markdown outline (headings and/or bullet list). End any line with " @a:<id>" to give that node a built-in illustration, or " @e:<emoji>" for one large emoji — e.g. "Launch @a:rocket". Ids: person, team, chat, idea, target, trophy, star, heart, warning, done, flag, clock, laptop, phone, mail, folder, book, chart, money, calendar, building, car, globe, rocket, house, pin, plane, coffee, plant, sun, camera, music, lock, key, health, gift. An unknown id is left as plain text rather than dropped.

space.description: Optional TabTree SPACE to put it in, by name — one of the user's spaces, or a TEAM space they are an editor of (every member then sees it). list_maps shows the spaces. Omit for the user's own library.

style.description: Optional look of the document. Omit it for the default.

background.description: Page background: dots (default), plain, grid, graph paper, ruled lines, isometric, paper, cream, kraft, aged, mist, sage, dawn, blueprint, slate (dark), chalkboard (dark).

font.description: Type family: grotesk (corporate), humanist (warm), condensed (dense), rounded (friendly), serif/garamond (editorial), didone (elegant), slab (sturdy), typewriter, mono (technical), hand (handwritten).

icons.description: How node icons are drawn: plain (default — a 20px line drawing), chip (the same drawing on a pill tinted with the branch colour), big (a 30px drawing on a larger pill). Only affects nodes that carry an icon. Travels with the map and into exported images.

palette.description: Branch colour palette (mind maps only): classic (default), ocean (cool blues), sunset (warm), forest (greens), berry (purples), nordic (calm cool), earth (terracotta and olive), vintage (faded warm), candy (bright and playful), muted (subdued, client-ready).

shape.description: Node shape: cards (default), line = underlined, plain = plain text.

skin.description: Structural skin — borders, shadows, corners: classic (default), soft (borderless, rounded, cushioned), flat (no shadows at all — for print and projection), paper (journal, soft warm shadows), ink (fine ink outline, no shadow), draft (square corners, dashed links — technical sketch), sticker (white cut-out ring, drop shadow — made to be posted), brutal (thick ink borders, hard offset shadows — the poster look), arcade (square corners, hard short shadows). Travels with the map and into exported images.

view.description: How TabTree opens it: map (default, a mind map), note (a page of text — the outline becomes headings and paragraphs, for meeting notes or a document), gantt (a timeline — give `dates`). It stays one document: the user can switch views at any time.

name: create_mindmap
